Code: `code/si/S8_robustness.R`. Each block repeats the main model under one
change: filtered tokens, another filtering threshold, another treatment of
the nomination limit, subsamples by classroom size, sex or grade, temporal
controls, a lagged placebo, and other ways of measuring rank.

For the regression tables, † denotes p < 0.10, * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, and *** p < 0.001.

```{r s8-setup}
```

#### Table S29. Higher to lower rank

This group includes ties in Social Rank, following the rule in the main analysis.

Specifications (4) and (5) are not estimable for this filtered sample. The fixed effects absorb all variation in its 116 observations.

```{r s8-filtered-high-to-low}
```

#### Table S30. Direct contrast between directions

The contrast is the higher-to-lower slope minus the lower-to-higher slope. The models use 370 directed decisions from 44 classrooms. The table reports classroom-clustered standard errors, 95% confidence intervals, and restricted wild-cluster bootstrap p-values (999 draws). The two specifications without fixed effects coincide and are shown in one row.

```{r s8-filtered-contrast}
```

```{r}
format_slope <- function(b, se) if_else(is.na(b), "n.e.", sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", b, se))
table_s30 %>%
  transmute(FE = fixed_effects, Model = pooled_model,
            `Lower to higher` = format_slope(lower_to_higher, lower_to_higher_se),
            `Higher to lower` = format_slope(higher_to_lower, higher_to_lower_se),
            Contrast = format_slope(contrast, contrast_se),
            `95% CI` = if_else(estimable, sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", ci_low, ci_high), "n.e."),
            `Cluster p` = round(cluster_p, 3), `Wild p` = round(wild_p, 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r s8-figure-s25}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.2
```

## 8.2 Filtering threshold and cutoff (Tables S31–S35)

"global" = one cutoff for all transfers (primary); "sender" = each child
keeps her own top share. n.e. (NA) marks models that cannot be estimated
(fewer than 10 residual degrees of freedom).

```{r s8-threshold-function}
```

```{r s8-thresholds}
```

### Table S35. Sensitivity to the global filter by nomination direction

Each row repeats the asymmetric-friendship analysis with a different share of transfers retained. A decision enters the filtered sample when both directions of the exchange survive. The sender count shows how many children still contribute at least two decisions. Standard errors are in parentheses. n.e. marks specifications with fewer than 10 residual degrees of freedom or without finite estimates. † p < 0.10, * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001.

```{r s8-asymmetric-thresholds}
```

#### Panel A. Lower-to-higher nominations

```{r}
knitr::kable(format_asymmetric_thresholds("Low to high"))
```

#### Panel B. Higher-to-lower nominations

```{r}
knitr::kable(format_asymmetric_thresholds("High to low"))
```

## 8.7 Sex and grade level (Tables S40–S51)

